primitives.name: Possession Priority
primitives.verbatim_quote: 136 WINNING FOOTBALL of the ball puts a team on the attack and that its opponents are then necessarily on their defense.
primitives.assumptions: The ball is the sole object of contested control; possession is binary (ball either held by attacker or defender).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when possession shifts mid-play, causing instantaneous tactical reclassification.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's discrete-event conformal inference framework, where possession change triggers posterior probability recalculation over outcome trees.

primitives.name: Position-Only Fallacy
primitives.verbatim_quote: A contrary—and I think equally mistaken—doctrine is that only position distinguishes between the two, and that a team is purely defending when it has the ball deep in its own territory.
primitives.assumptions: Defensive/attacking status is determined solely by spatial zone; possession is irrelevant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in transition scenarios where deep-possession teams still attempt forward passes.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state-transition logic, where position-only models fail to capture dynamic possession-based role changes.
layer2.telemetry: Zone occupancy metrics, defensive depth indices

primitives.name: Middle Ground
primitives.verbatim_quote: I take the middle ground which declares that possession and position are both factors to be considered, with the qualification that the attack always inclines toward the team which holds the ball, wherever it is.
primitives.assumptions: Tactical classification is bivariate (possession-state space); the direction of inclination is probabilistic, not deterministic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ambiguity arises at the boundary between offensive and defensive phases, where neither factor clearly dominates.

layer2.mapping: Derives GSI's joint possession-zone Bayesian network, where conditional probabilities update based on simultaneous possession and location.
layer2.telemetry: Conditional win probabilities given possession and zone

primitives.name: Scoring Imperative
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is seemingly self-evident in that no score can be made without possession of the ball, and that the very word attack involves the idea of scoring and the word defense implies the prevention of a score as the immediate objective.
primitives.assumptions: All plays are evaluated against a binary scoring outcome; defense is a zero-sum constraint on offense.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when defensive strategies prioritize possession retention over aggressive tackling, deferring scoring pressure.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's utility-maximizing agent model, where attackers maximize scoring odds and defenders minimize opponent's utility function.
layer2.telemetry: Expected goals (xG), expected points per drive

reasoning_traces.think:
The four primitives form a hierarchical lattice: possession priority dictates immediate action, while the position-only fallacy represents a lower-dimensional projection that ignores temporal dynamics. Middle ground reconciles these by introducing a bivariate state space (possession, position) with a directional bias favoring the ball carrier. Scoring imperative anchors the system by linking every action to the terminal outcome of goal-scoring. The lattice breaks down at transitions because possession shifts are non-differentiable events, creating a need for conformal inference to handle the resulting singularities. In practice, this means that defensive systems must be robust to sudden possession loss, while offensive systems should maintain options even after losing the ball. The primitives also reveal a duality: a play can be viewed as an attack from the perspective of the ball carrier and as a defense from the receiver's perspective, leading to coupled differential games.
